description: Config for an atolla headless player. `atolla init` creates the config file, at /etc/atolla/player.json by default. The player reads it only when it starts, so restart the player after changing it, e.g.: `sudo systemctl restart atolla`.

$schema.description: Link to this schema. Editors that support JSON schema use it to validate the file and describe each field.

audioDevice.description: Audio output to play through. `default` lets the system choose and `none` plays nothing while still keeping in sync. Use `atolla outputs` to list the available options.

audioPort.description: Port this player streams audio on. While it's the source, other players in its group connect to it.

bindAddress.description: IPv4 address the control server, clock and audio stream listen on. `0.0.0.0` listens on every network interface.

clockPort.description: Port this player serves its clock on. While it's the source, other players in its group follow this clock to stay in step.

dataDir.description: Directory for atolla to write data to such as cached tracks and saved state.

mediaCacheGb.description: Gigabytes of tracks to available in cache before evicted. Required for offline playback when this player is the controller.

name.description: Name the app shows for this player.

port.description: Port the control server listens on that the app connects to.

streamLatencyMs.description: How far ahead the source schedules audio, in milliseconds. Play, resume, skip and seek each wait this long before you hear them. If a speaker plays short bursts and then silence, raise it by 50. Use the same value on every speaker in a group, because only the source's value is used. Keep it under 500, or the controls in the app will feel slow.

title: atolla player config
